record.paper_title: Progresses on Some Open Problems Related to Infinitely Many Symmetries
record.original_question: For nonlinear physical systems described by partial differential equations and therefore having infinitely many degrees of freedom, are the currently known infinitely many symmetries complete, or are there additional undiscovered symmetries beyond the standard known families?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider nonlinear physical systems described by partial differential equations (PDEs), which possess infinitely many degrees of freedom. For an integrable PDE system, one can typically construct two infinite hierarchies of generalized (Lie–Bäcklund) symmetries: the so-called K-symmetries $K_n$, obtained by repeatedly applying a recursion operator to a seed symmetry such as the translation symmetry, and the τ-symmetries $\tau_n$, which depend explicitly on the independent variables and generate a centerless Kac–Moody–Virasoro–type algebra together with the $K_n$. These two families are conventionally regarded as constituting the complete set of higher symmetries of the system.

Question: Given an integrable nonlinear PDE with infinitely many degrees of freedom, is the union of its currently known infinite hierarchies of symmetries (the $K_n$-symmetries and $\tau_n$-symmetries, together with point symmetries) complete, in the sense that every generalized symmetry of the system is a (possibly infinite) linear combination of members of these hierarchies? Equivalently, do there exist additional, genuinely independent symmetries of such systems that lie outside the standard $K$- and $\tau$-hierarchies?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work argues that the customarily known infinite K- and τ-symmetry hierarchies of integrable PDEs are in fact incomplete: when restricted to multi-wave solutions they collapse to a finite-dimensional space and are shown to be linear combinations of finitely many wave-parameter translation symmetries, indicating that additional independent symmetries (e.g., from multi-wave parameter translations) must be included. A fully general classification of all symmetries for arbitrary integrable PDEs is not established, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Progresses on some open problems related to infinitely many symmetries
status_evidence.snippet: The purportedly infinite K-symmetries and τ-symmetries are, in reality, incomplete, as evidenced by their transformation into a finite set when applied to specific n-wave solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Known infinite symmetry hierarchies are shown to be incomplete on multi-wave solutions, indicating additional symmetries beyond the standard families.

status_evidence.title: Progresses on Some Open Problems Related to Infinitely Many Symmetries (MDPI Mathematics)
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates five open problems related to infinite symmetries of integrable systems via multi-wave solutions, including the completeness problem.
status_evidence.claim: The completeness of known symmetries is treated as one of several open problems with partial progress.
